interest: Sale of U.S. surplus property in occupied Japan, 1946–49.
keywords: Office of the Foreign Liquidation Commissioner
Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: State Department Decimal File 894.24 FLC (File 1738) documents the postwar activities, bulk sales negotiations, and operational close-out of the Office of the Foreign Liquidation Commissioner (OFLC) in Japan and adjacent East Asian theaters between September 1946 and July 1949. The collection centers on the execution and amendment of major bilateral agreements between the United States and the Japanese Government—negotiated through and certified by General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)—for the bulk transfer of tens of millions of dollars in civilian-type military surplus property to support Japanese economic recovery. The file traces foundational contracts like Agreement No. W-FLC(CH-II)-500, interagency coordination regarding scrap metal disposals and National Advisory Council credit ceilings, amendments adjusting contractual language to align with Japan's post-imperial constitutional status, and delicate negotiations on currency conversion rates for Japan's national budget. It also details regional logistics and surplus coordination involving Korea, Hawaii, the Ryukyu Islands, and Nationalist China, alongside localized disposals such as the salvage sale of a submerged aircraft rescue boat in Tokyo Bay and the administrative close-out of OFLC's Tokyo mission in early 1949.

subfiles.about: Establishes general terms and conditions for the sale of U.S. civilian-type military surplus supplies in Japan to the Imperial Japanese Government under SCAP approval.
subfiles.from: William E. Vogelback (Central Field Commissioner for Pacific and China, OFLC)
subfiles.summary: Letter agreement for selling U.S. surplus property to Japan, accepted November 5, 1946 by K. Tsukada and certified by SCAP.
subfiles.title: Letter of Agreement for Sale of U.S. Surplus Property to Imperial Japanese Government
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government (accepted by K. Tsukada, Director General, Board of Trade; approved by Brigadier General W. F. Marquat, ESS, SCAP)

subfiles.about: Transmits duplicate and copies of the executed surplus property letter of agreement between OFLC and the Imperial Japanese Government.
subfiles.from: Colonel John B. Cooley (Adjutant General, GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: SCAP returns the signed surplus property agreement to OFLC Tokyo.
subfiles.title: SCAP Transmittal of Signed Surplus Property Agreement to OFLC Tokyo
subfiles.to: Assistant Field Commissioner for China and Eastern Asia, OFLC Tokyo

subfiles.about: Offers editorial corrections and substantive comments on a draft report to the National Advisory Council Staff Committee concerning surplus property.
subfiles.summary: E. F. Smith suggests revising surplus figures in a report to the NAC Staff Committee.
subfiles.title: OFLC Memorandum on Proposed Report to the NAC Staff Committee
subfiles.to: Hale T. Shenefield (LP, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of the formal surplus property sales agreement No. W-FLC(CH-II)-500 concluded between the United States and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Carre sends State a copy of surplus sale agreement No. W-FLC(CH-II)-500.
subfiles.title: OFLC Memorandum Transmitting Bulk Sale Agreement No. W-FLC(CH-II)-500
subfiles.to: Hale T. Shenefield (LP, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Sets out comprehensive contractual terms for the bulk sale of up to approximately $50 million procurement cost of U.S. surplus property in Japan at 30 percent of cost.
subfiles.from: Major George S. Hammonds (Assistant Field Commissioner for China and Eastern Asia, OFLC, United States)
subfiles.summary: Agreement selling about $50 million of U.S. surplus in Japan at 30 percent of cost, excluding combat materiel and vessels.
subfiles.title: Agreement Between the United States and Japan for the Sale of Certain Surplus Property (No. W-FLC(CH-II)-500)
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government (signed by K. Tsukada, Director General, Board of Trade; approved by Brigadier General W. F. Marquat, ESS, SCAP)

subfiles.about: Inquires whether surplus disposals in Japan and Korea fall under the Civilian Supply Program or NAC authorizations, and queries scrap metal disposal rules.
subfiles.from: WDGSF/D (signed Lutes, War Department General Staff)
subfiles.summary: Lutes asks CINCFE the authority for surplus transfers and whether scrap went to Korea and Japan.
subfiles.title: War Department Message on Civilian Supply Program and Scrap Disposals

subfiles.about: Instructs USPOLAD Tokyo to forward Form FS-358 pay and allowance records for departing OFLC personnel to the Division of Finance.
subfiles.from: Department of State (signed JBS for the Acting Secretary)
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-30 on submitting pay cards for OFLC personnel leaving post.
subfiles.title: State Department Airgram A-30 on Decentralization of Pay and Allowance Cards

subfiles.about: Reports the execution of the delivery contract for the eight and one-third group military program between CINCFE and the Chinese Government.
subfiles.summary: OFLC Tokyo reports the delivery contract for the eight and one-third group air program signed with China, January 1948.
subfiles.title: Telegram from OFLC Tokyo on Delivery Contract for Eight and One-Third Group Program
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (OFLC Washington for Connolly)

subfiles.about: Clarifies OFLC Nassau's position on air service agreements, weather facilities, and transferred installations in Saigon.
subfiles.summary: OFLC Nassau recognizes the Saigon air facilities agreement and disclaims further knowledge.
subfiles.title: Telegram from OFLC Nassau Concerning Saigon Air Facilities

subfiles.about: Reports on excess military property shipped from Hawaii to Korea and contractual issues concerning its purchase by USAHQIK.
subfiles.summary: OFLC Tokyo asks whether to amend contracts so the Army in Korea can buy surplus shipped from Hawaii.
subfiles.title: Telegram from OFLC Tokyo on Surplus Property from Hawaii Desired by USAHQIK

subfiles.about: Queries whether civilian import requirements under Project 160 for the Ryukyus can be sourced from Far Eastern surplus before procuring in the U.S.
subfiles.from: CSCAD (Civil Affairs Division, War Department / Maj Spreyer)
subfiles.summary: War Department asks whether Ryukyus import needs could be met from Far East surplus.
subfiles.title: War Department Message on Ryukyus Civilian Import Requirements (Project 160)

subfiles.about: Reports an unpaid $100 million claim against the Chinese Government for aircraft engines and supplies under June 1948 CFLC contracts.
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy / Diplomatic Mission (transmitted via Washington)
subfiles.summary: CFLC Shanghai refers a $100 million claim against China for aircraft engines and supplies to the Embassy.
subfiles.title: Telegram on CFLC $100 Million Claim Against Chinese Government

subfiles.about: Cancels prior signal reference and advises that Auster Mark 5 aircraft and engines will be transferred to another Royal Air Force command.
subfiles.from: Tokyo (Far East Air Forces / TAKO BORIN)
subfiles.summary: FEAF message moving Lend-Lease Auster aircraft to another RAF command.
subfiles.title: Army Message QZ802 on Transfer of Lend-Lease Auster Aircraft to RAF Command

subfiles.about: Requests Munitions Division clearance for the private sale of an Army aircraft rescue boat (P-716) in Tokyo to an American citizen.
subfiles.from: Captain C. O. Sullinger (per Lt. Nevling, OFLC)
subfiles.summary: OFLC asks clearance to sell rescue boat P-716 to William Brethwaite for pleasure use.
subfiles.title: OFLC Memorandum Requesting Clearance to Sell Army Rescue Boat P-716
subfiles.to: E. T. Cummins (Munitions Division, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Details the history, salvage status, and proposed $500 sale of submerged 63-foot rescue craft P-716 to William Brethwaite.
subfiles.summary: Akin reports rotted rescue boat P-716, dredged from Tokyo Bay, approved for sale to William Brethwaite for $500.
subfiles.title: OFLC Tokyo Cable Z-35652 on Salvage and Sale of Rescue Boat P-716

subfiles.about: Urges OFLC Tokyo to cable final figures from its blotter account immediately upon the office's close-out date of March 19, 1949.
subfiles.from: Department of State (signed Acheson / Hyssong for OFLC)
subfiles.summary: Acheson urges final figures before OFLC Tokyo closes on March 19, 1949.
subfiles.title: State Department Airgram A-27 on OFLC Tokyo Close-Out and Final Blotter Account

subfiles.about: Reports that OFLC representatives and SCAP ESS have approved draft contract amendments modernizing Japan's title and adding a recent contract.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports SCAP approval of surplus contract amendments, including deleting 'Imperial'.
subfiles.title: Telegram C 68689DA on Amendments to Japanese Surplus Property Sales Contract

subfiles.about: Reports on preliminary consultations between OFLC officials and Japanese Commerce Minister Inagaki regarding proposed surplus contract amendments.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Commerce Minister Inagaki will consult colleagues on the contract amendments.
subfiles.title: Telegram 83 on Consultation with Commerce Minister Inagaki Regarding Contract Amendments

subfiles.about: Proposes an exchange rate clause in the surplus property amendment to enable yen funding in the Japanese budget for the upcoming fiscal year.
subfiles.summary: Sebald proposes an exchange rate clause so surplus payments fit Japan's budget.
subfiles.title: Telegram 88 on Foreign Exchange Rate Clause for Japanese Surplus Property Contract
subfiles.to: Department of Army / Department of State

subfiles.about: Requests approval for trade representative Harold Maynard to return from New Delhi via the Middle East to discuss Japanese-Turkish trade.
subfiles.summary: Sebald asks that Harold Maynard return via Turkey for trade talks.
subfiles.title: Telegram 95 on Trade Representative Harold Maynard's Mission to New Delhi and Middle East

subfiles.about: Inquires about missing military efficiency reports for Lt. Col. Alfred K. Akin covering his service with OFLC Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Message on missing efficiency reports for Lt. Col. Alfred K. Akin.
subfiles.title: Army Message Z-15426 Inquiring on Missing Efficiency Reports for Lt. Col. Alfred K. Akin
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Attn: Francis T. Murphy, OFLC Audit Unit)
